name: Charles I of England
role: King of England, Scotland and Ireland (1625–1649)
summary: Charles I upheld a hereditary monarchy in which the king held the powers of war, appointment and assent within a mixed constitution of King, Lords and Commons, and rejected Parliament's claims to share in them. He backed an episcopal, uniform established church under Laud, ruled eleven years without calling an English Parliament, and denied that the people have a share in government. He refused to recognise the court that tried him in 1649.

notes: Eikon Basilike was not used (attributed to Gauden). Laws he assented to under pressure (Petition of Right, Triennial Act, Strafford's attainder) are not counted as his positions. Themes searched: government, church, economy and taxation, world (the Answer's alliance clause, the Scottish wars), liberty and society; his surviving texts and the trial and scaffold speeches say little beyond constitution, church and militia, so most statements are null. Record answers rest on scholarly reports (Hyde, James), so are medium at most; sources that only cited Wikipedia in the first pass were dropped and the answers re-based on texts and scholarship.

booksNotUsed.reason: Eikon Basilike was published under his name but is attributed by modern scholarship to John Gauden, so it is not shown to be words he delivered as his own.
